inputs.goal: port the admin app from Flask to FastAPI in verifiable slices

slices.name: authentication_layer
slices.description: Migrate Flask authentication decorators and middleware to FastAPI dependencies and security models
slices.verification: Ensure all existing auth endpoints work with new FastAPI security models

slices.name: route_definitions
slices.description: Convert Flask routes to FastAPI route decorators with proper path parameters and HTTP methods
slices.verification: All original endpoints accessible with same URLs and HTTP methods

slices.name: request_response_handling
slices.description: Replace Flask request/response objects with FastAPI's Request and Response models
slices.verification: All API responses maintain identical structure and status codes

slices.name: database_integration
slices.description: Migrate SQLAlchemy models and session management to FastAPI dependency injection pattern
slices.verification: Database operations work identically with new dependency injection approach

slices.name: error_handling
slices.description: Convert Flask error handlers to FastAPI exception handlers and custom exceptions
slices.verification: All error cases produce same error responses as original Flask app

risk_map.authentication_layer: High - Security model changes could break existing auth flows
risk_map.route_definitions: Medium - Path parameter handling differences between Flask and FastAPI
risk_map.request_response_handling: Medium - Response format changes might affect client integrations
risk_map.database_integration: High - Dependency injection pattern changes could cause data access issues
risk_map.error_handling: Low - Exception handling is generally more straightforward in FastAPI

port-slice.intake.summary: Porting admin app from Flask to FastAPI in verifiable slices. Starting with authentication_layer slice, which has high risk due to security model changes but is critical for subsequent slices. Will migrate Flask decorators and middleware to FastAPI dependencies, ensuring existing auth endpoints work with new security models. Next will convert route definitions using FastAPI decorators, then replace request/response objects, followed by database integration via dependency injection, and finally implement error handling with exception handlers.
